notes.text: Rasmus Sandin is on long-term injured reserve (knee surgery) and has missed the last 13 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Timothy Liljegren has taken his spot beside Martin Fehérváry. That pair has had 46% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 86:48 together.
Jakob Chychrun has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 17 games, up from 8% last season.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 6 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Conor Geekie takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Emil Lilleberg is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside McDonagh and Crozier.
Anthony Cirelli is day to day (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. Nikita Kucherov has taken his spot beside Jake Guentzel and Brandon Hagel.
Brayden Point is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Brandon Hagel has taken his spot beside Nikita Kucherov and Jake Guentzel.
Erik Černák is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. Max Crozier has taken his spot beside Ryan McDonagh.
Gage Goncalves returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Sam O'Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Yanni Gourde and Jake Guentzel.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

story.head: The Capitals give up shots, and the Lightning take them
paras: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Tampa Bay on Oct 3. The Lightning have won two in a row, while the Capitals (10-7-0) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Thursday. Going in, the Capitals are fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Bolts first in the Atlantic (tied for fifth).
The Capitals’ record (.588) is about what their chances are worth. The Lightning’s record (.737) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.669), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Capitals get the league’s best looks (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (27th), so the Lightning could find some good looks against them, who give up plenty of them. The Lightning keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd) and rarely ice the puck (4th), but don't block many shots (29th). Tampa Bay has scored 3.89 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Lightning are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Capitals.

Dylan Strome (3 G / 12 A / 15 P in 17 GP) leads the Capitals in scoring, and Alex Tuch (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. Nikita Kucherov (8 G / 20 A / 28 P in 19 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Brandon Hagel (13 G / 11 A / 24 P in 19 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and six goals in ten games against Washington since 2023-24.
Logan Thompson (7-5-0 / .889 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Washington, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (9-4-1 / .884 SV% in 14 GS) for Tampa Bay.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kyrou, Strome and Leonard.
